summary: Independent review requires revision. The paper states effective counting, interpolation and Diophantine applications, but the extraction needs source-proof repairs for local resultants and general position, exact imported statements, and complete definition APIs. Clear statement, ownership and coverage corrections are applied; none is a formalization. The published main theorems remain targets, not results disproved merely by a gap in the supplied proof.

items.name: Foliated affine variety, leaves and ξ-balls
items.statement: M ⊂ 𝔸^N_K an irreducible affine variety over a number field K with the Euclidean metric and balls B_R; ξ = (ξ₁,…,ξ_n) commuting, generically independent rational vector fields over K generating a singular foliation F, with Σ_F the polar loci and dependency locus; for p ∉ Σ_F the leaf germ L_p with ξ-chart φ_p : (ℂⁿ,0) → L_p, ∂φ_p/∂x_i = ξ_i; ξ-balls B = φ_p(B) and the notation A^δ for radius δ^{-1}r.
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

api.name: FoliatedAffine.singularLocus
api.statement: The singular locus is the union of pole loci and failure of rank n.

api.name: FoliatedAffine.chart_derivative
api.statement: At a regular base point, the chart sends 0 to the point and its ith partial derivative equals ξi along the chart.

api.name: FoliatedAffine.ball_rescale
api.statement: Replacing the chart ball radius r by r/δ gives the paper’s B^δ.

unitTests.name: FoliatedAffine.test_coordinate_fields
unitTests.statement: On A² with ξ1=∂x, ξ2=∂y, the singular locus is empty and charts are translations.

unitTests.name: FoliatedAffine.test_dependent_fields
unitTests.statement: The pair (∂x,2∂x) on A² is rank deficient everywhere and does not define a regular two-dimensional leaf.

unitTests.name: FoliatedAffine.test_half_ball
unitTests.statement: B² has half the ξ-coordinate radius of B, not twice the radius.

uses.how: Controls the regular chart, derivative operations and shrinking convention.

items.name: Complexity of polynomials, varieties and vector fields
items.statement: δ(P) = max(deg P, h(P)); for V ⊂ M, deg V in the standard projective embedding and h(V) the height of its Chow coordinates; δ_M = max([K:ℚ], deg M, h(M)), δ(V) = max(δ_M, deg V, h(V)), δ(ξ) = max(δ_M, deg ξ, h(ξ)).
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

api.name: FoliationComplexity.polynomial_eq_max
api.statement: δP=max(deg P,h(P)) with the fixed absolute coefficient height.

api.name: FoliationComplexity.variety_ge_base
api.statement: δV≥δM for a subvariety of the fixed ambient data.

api.name: FoliationComplexity.vectorField_coordinates
api.statement: Record degree and height bounds for the rational coordinate functions of ξ on the chosen localized affine presentation.

unitTests.name: FoliationComplexity.test_rational_linear
unitTests.statement: For P(T)=T over Q, δP=1.

unitTests.name: FoliationComplexity.test_base_field_degree

unitTests.name: FoliationComplexity.test_zero_height_degree
unitTests.statement: For P(T)=T^m with m≥1, h(P)=0 and δP=m.

items.name: Absolute logarithmic height of an algebraic element
items.statement: For an algebraic element x in a characteristic-zero field, h_abs(x) is log of the multiplicative height of the generator in Q(x), raised to 1/[Q(x):Q]. This is the existing scalar construction. The minimal-polynomial formula and the tuple maximum used by the paper are the separate comparison item /53.
items.note: Read NumberTheory/Height/NumberField.lean:135–147 at 082e2d3. Projectivization.logHeight is a relative projective height and does not supply the original combined item. The scalar construction itself already exists; do not rebuild it.

api.name: AbsoluteHeight.multiplicative_eq_exp
api.statement: For algebraic x the multiplicative height is exp of the logarithmic height.

api.name: AbsoluteHeight.minpoly_comparison

items.name: The unlikely intersection locus Σ_V
items.statement: For V ⊂ M pure-dimensional of codimension ≤ n, Σ_V = Σ_F ∪ {p : dim(V ∩ L_p) > n − codim V} (4); for arbitrary codimension Σ = Σ_F ∪ {p : dim(V ∩ L_p) > 0} (6).
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

api.name: UnlikelyIntersection.mem_regular_iff
api.statement: Outside ΣF, membership means dim(V∩Lp)>n−codim V.

api.name: UnlikelyIntersection.singular_subset
api.statement: ΣF is included in ΣV.

api.name: UnlikelyIntersection.isolated_variant
api.statement: The arbitrary-codimension variant uses dim(V∩Lp)>0, separately from ΣV.

unitTests.name: UnlikelyIntersection.test_transverse_line
unitTests.statement: For ξ=∂x on A² and V={x=0}, ΣV is empty.

unitTests.name: UnlikelyIntersection.test_invariant_line
unitTests.statement: For ξ=∂x and V={y=0}, ΣV={y=0}.

unitTests.name: UnlikelyIntersection.test_full_rank_point
unitTests.statement: For the coordinate two-dimensional foliation and V={(0,0)}, the intersection has expected dimension zero and ΣV is empty.

uses.how: Specifies which distance controls each theorem.

items.name: Weierstrass polydiscs
items.statement: For an analytic X ⊂ B of pure dimension m and unitary coordinates x = z × w, a polydisc Δ = Δ_z × Δ_w with Δ̄ ⊂ B, dim Δ_z = m and X ∩ (Δ̄_z × ∂Δ_w) = ∅; then Δ ∩ X → Δ_z is a proper ramified cover of degree e(Δ, X).
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

api.name: WeierstrassPolydisc.boundary_avoiding
api.statement: In unitary z,w coordinates, X avoids Δ̄z×∂Δw and dim z=dim X.

api.name: WeierstrassPolydisc.projection_finite
api.statement: Projection of X∩Δ to Δz is finite proper with degree e.

api.name: WeierstrassPolydisc.degree_fibre
api.statement: The fibre multiplicities sum to e, including ramified fibres.

unitTests.name: WeierstrassPolydisc.test_flat_graph
unitTests.statement: For X={w=0}, any product disc centred at 0 inside the domain is Weierstrass of degree 1.

unitTests.name: WeierstrassPolydisc.test_branched_double
unitTests.statement: For X={w²=z}, choose radii with sqrt(rz)<rw; the projection has degree 2 including at z=0.

unitTests.name: WeierstrassPolydisc.test_boundary_intersection
unitTests.statement: If X meets Δ̄z×∂Δw, the selected product disc is not a Weierstrass polydisc for X.

uses.how: Produces the finite fibres, multiplicities and analytic expansion domain.

items.name: Theorem 1 (intersections of a leaf ball with a variety)
items.statement: If codim V = n and B ⊂ B_R is a ξ-ball of radius ≤ R, then #(B² ∩ V) = poly(δ_ξ, δ_V, log R, log dist^{-1}(B, Σ_V)), counted with multiplicity.
items.locator: Theorem 1, p.3; proof §5.1, pp.16–17, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Induction with Theorem 2 in dimension n: a Weierstrass polydisc for V(P₁,…,P_{n−1}), the analytic resultant of P_n, a Jensen-type zero count and lower bounds via multiplicity operators (Lemma 11, Corollary 14). Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Corollary 2 (arbitrary codimension)
items.statement: For V of arbitrary codimension, #(B² ∩ V) = poly(δ_ξ, δ_V, log R, log dist^{-1}(B, Σ)) with Σ as in (6).
items.locator: Corollary 2, p.3; proof §5.2, p.17, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Proposition 22 with m = n, then Theorem 1. Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Theorem 2 (covering by Weierstrass polydiscs)
items.statement: If codim V ≤ n and B ⊂ B_R is a ξ-ball of radius ≤ R, there are Weierstrass polydiscs {Δ_α ⊂ B} for B ∩ V with ⋃Δ_α² ⊃ B² and #{Δ_α}, max_α e(B ∩ V, Δ_α) = poly(δ_ξ, δ_V, log R, log dist^{-1}(B, Σ_V)).
items.locator: Theorem 2, p.4; proof §5.3, p.17, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Corollary 18 reduces to bounding vol(B ∩ V), which Crofton reduces to Theorem 1 for linear subfoliations in general position. Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Theorem 3: algebraic points covered by blocks from nearby leaves
items.statement: With the foliated data /1, regular K-map Φ : M → C^ℓ, K-subvariety V, and ξ-ball B ⊂ B_R of ξ-radius at most R, put A=Φ(B²∩V). For g≥1, h≥0 and ε>0, there are subvarieties defined and irreducible over Q (not necessarily geometrically irreducible) Wα of C^ℓ covering A(g,h) of /56, with dist(B,Σ(V,Wα;Φ))<ε, and number and complexities bounded by poly(δξ,δV,δΦ,g,h,log R,log ε^−1). Σ is /55. All logarithmic size parameters are bounded below by a fixed positive constant for the polynomial-bound convention.
items.locator: Definition 4 and Theorem 3, p.4; proof §6.2, pp.19–20, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: The published page 4 says Q-subvarieties, not Qbar-subvarieties. Degree means joint field degree. This is a stated target with unresolved proof dependencies /15, /23, /80; see review gaps, not an accepted proof.

items.name: Corollary 6 (no blocks on any leaf)
items.statement: If Φ|_{L_p ∩ V} is finite and Φ(L_p ∩ V) contains no algebraic curve germ for every p, then #A(g,h) = poly_ℓ(δ_ξ, δ_V, δ_Φ, log R, g, h).
items.locator: Corollary 6, p.5, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Wilkie's conjecture for restricted elementary functions (Binyamini–Novikov)
items.statement: For A ⊂ ℝ^m definable in ℝ_RE = (ℝ, <, +, ·, exp|_{[0,1]}, sin|_{[0,π]}), #A^trans(g,h) = poly_{A,g}(h), where A^alg is the union of positive-dimensional connected semialgebraic subsets and A^trans = A ∖ A^alg.
items.locator: §1.4, (14), p.5, citing Binyamini–Novikov [12, Thm. 2], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Theorem 4 (sharp dependence on the degree)
items.statement: If A ⊂ ℝ^m is ℝ_RE-definable, then #A^trans(g,h) = poly_A(g,h).
items.locator: Theorem 4, p.5, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Replace [12, Prop. 12] by Proposition 28. Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Multiplicity operators (Binyamini–Novikov)
items.statement: The basic multiplicity operators of order k for an n-tuple F of holomorphic germs are the determinantal polynomial differential operators in its k-jet, as constructed in Binyamini–Novikov [10]. Use basic operators only, not their convex hull, to retain number-field height bounds. Zero multiplicity means a nonzero germ value; a nonisolated common zero has infinite multiplicity.
items.locator: §2, Proposition 7, p.9; §2.2, Lemma 12, p.10, citing [10], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Definition/construction only. Vanishing criterion and arithmetic complexity are /68 and /67. Source E9 corrects the nonisolated-zero convention. A full determinant-level construction and API remain required from [10].

api.name: BasicMultiplicityOperator.depends_on_jet
api.statement: An order-k basic operator depends polynomially only on the k-jet of F.

api.name: BasicMultiplicityOperator.vanishing_criterion
api.statement: Import /68 for the simultaneous vanishing criterion.

api.name: BasicMultiplicityOperator.along_fields
api.statement: For commuting coordinate fields, the leafwise operator agrees with the usual partial-derivative operator.

unitTests.name: BasicMultiplicityOperator.test_simple_zero
unitTests.statement: For F=(z1,…,zn), the origin has multiplicity 1, so some order-1 basic operator is nonzero.

unitTests.name: BasicMultiplicityOperator.test_double_zero
unitTests.statement: For the one-variable F=z², all order-1 operators vanish and some order-2 operator is nonzero.

unitTests.name: BasicMultiplicityOperator.test_nonisolated_zero
unitTests.statement: For F=(z,0) in two variables, all finite-order basic operators vanish; the multiplicity is infinite.

uses.how: Determines local intersection multiplicity and bounds heights of its tests.

items.name: Local lower bound away from exceptional coordinate discs
items.statement: If F : B → D(1)ⁿ with s = |M₀^{(k)}F| ≠ 0, then for unit ℓ ∈ (ℂⁿ)* and 0 < ρ < s there are a ball of radius ≥ s/poly_n(k) and ≤ k discs U_ρ of total radius poly_n(k)ρ with log‖F(z)‖ ≥ (k+1) log ρ − poly_n(k) off ℓ^{-1}(U_ρ) (Lemma 8).
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Local resultant lower bound with fibre containment
items.statement: Let F:B→D(1)^n, Γ={F1=…=F(n−1)=0}, and s=|M0^(k)F|>0. Choose the ball B′ and exceptional set Uρ from Lemma 8 for the z-coordinate. If Δ is a Weierstrass polydisc of degree μ and every point of the fibre over z lies in B′, then outside Uρ one has log|RΔ,Γ(Fn)(z)|≥μ((k+1)logρ−poly_n(k)). The estimate holds only where the resultant is defined and the fibre-containment hypothesis holds.
items.locator: Definition 10 and Lemma 11, p.10, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Corrected E10 by adding precisely the hypothesis used in the product proof. The printed arbitrary-Δ version is false. Constructing all local polydiscs required in §5.1 with this property and quantitative radii remains G1; no claim that this repairs the whole theorem is made.

items.name: Gabrielov–Khovanskii multiplicity estimate
items.statement: For P = (P₁,…,P_n) and p ∈ M ∖ Σ_V(P), mult_p P < poly(deg ξ, deg P) (Theorem 5 [26]).
items.locator: Theorem 5, p.10, citing Gabrielov–Khovanskii [26], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Complexity of the unlikely-intersection locus
items.statement: For a complete intersection V=V(P1,…,Pm), m≤n, the unlikely-intersection locus has δ(ΣV)≤poly(δξ,δV). On the regular foliation locus when m=n, equations are supplied by all basic multiplicity operators of a polynomially bounded order; restore ΣF globally.
items.note: The proof through the displayed generators first bounds complexity using δP. Passing to intrinsic δV requires a bounded normalized defining tuple; keep this obligation explicit, in particular for the Corollary-14 application E23.

items.name: Brownawell's Diophantine Łojasiewicz inequality
items.statement: If polynomials f_j over a number field with degrees and heights ≤ δ cut out Z set-theoretically, then max_j |f_j(p)| ≥ (dist(p, Z)/c)^{poly(δ)} on a bounded region, with effective constants ([20]).
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 14, p.11; §1.6.1, p.7, citing Brownawell [20], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: An effective Nullstellensatz-type inequality from transcendence theory. Routed to DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence DT.3 as a source.

items.name: Packing an analytic set using its volume
items.statement: Let X be a closed pure m-dimensional complex analytic subset of the unit ball and 0<ε≤1. Then S(X∩B²,ε)≤2^(2m)c(m)^−1 vol(X) ε^(−2m), by the Lelong lower bound vol(X∩B(p,ε/2))≥c(m)(ε/2)^(2m) for p∈X∩B².
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: A complementary ball controlled by analytic volume
items.statement: For a pure m-dimensional complex analytic X in the unit ball of C^n with m<n and finite volume, there is a ball disjoint from S¹·X whose reciprocal radius is bounded by Cn(1+vol X)^(1/(2n−2m−1)). Use the packing estimate in a smaller concentric ball; the 1+ convention also covers empty or very small-volume sets.
items.note: Require m<n. The printed bound suppresses the lower cutoff; the full-dimensional case has no complementary ball and must be handled separately in the covering corollary. Source E20 records both the full-dimensional and vanishing-volume failures.

items.name: Linear subfoliations and polynomial reparametrisation
items.statement: For 1≤k≤n, let A(n,k) be the full-rank matrix locus. On L_k M=A(n,k)×M, extend each commuting vector field by the linear combination sum_j α_ji ξ_j, keeping α constant. Leaves project to k-dimensional linear subfoliations in the ξ-charts.
items.note: Full-rank matrices form a quasi-affine open locus, not generally an affine variety without an auxiliary chart cover. The localized-chart arithmetic and comparison are a design obligation.

api.name: LinearSubfoliation.rank_required
api.statement: Choose an n×k coefficient matrix of rank k and form the k constant linear combinations of ξ.

api.name: LinearSubfoliation.commuting
api.statement: Constant combinations of commuting fields commute.

api.name: LinearSubfoliation.coordinate_image
api.statement: The projected leaf germ is the image of the chosen linear map in the ξ-chart.

unitTests.name: LinearSubfoliation.test_identity_matrix
unitTests.statement: For k=n and the identity matrix recover the original fields.

unitTests.name: LinearSubfoliation.test_first_coordinate
unitTests.statement: For coordinate fields on A² and column (1,0), leaves project to horizontal lines.

unitTests.name: LinearSubfoliation.test_zero_column
unitTests.statement: A zero column does not provide a rank-one subfoliation.

uses.how: Provides lower-dimensional leaves used in the induction.

items.name: General position (§4.2, Lemmas 19–20)
items.statement: There are M̃ = N × M and fields ξ̃ generating the same foliation with charts close to the identity (‖Φ_{a,p} − id‖_{B²} < 0.1), deg ξ̃ = deg ξ + O(1), h(ξ̃) = poly(δ_ξ, deg V), and no new unlikely intersections on linear subfoliations (π_M(Σ_Ṽ) ⊂ Σ_V).
items.locator: §4.2, (42)–(44), p.13; Lemmas 19–20, p.14, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6 (misprint E2)
items.note: The requested simultaneous general-position construction depends on /80. Restrict the exceptional incidence to good points as E2 requires, and repair the image/inverse mismatch E12 before treating the proof as established.

items.name: Proposition 22 (a well-chosen complete intersection)
items.statement: For a containing complete intersection W⊃V of pure codimension m to exist globally it is necessary that m≤codim_M V. In this range, the intended effective statement asks for δW≤poly(δξ,δV) and, off ΣF, bad-intersection locus equal to {p:dim(V∩Lp)>n−m}. The unrestricted statement for 0≤m≤dim M is false. Uses requiring larger m need a separately proved construction on the good locus after removing forced components; that construction is a recorded gap.
items.locator: Proposition 22 and proof, p.15, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6 (misprint E2)
items.note: E11 gives a dimension counterexample. Adding m≤codim V does not by itself establish the equality or the applications in §5.2 and Proposition 29. A repaired proof must also address E2 and restore the singular locus.

items.name: Jensen's inequality for zeros
items.statement: Let 0 < r < R, M ≥ 1 and f : C → C be analytic on a neighbourhood of the closed disc with centre c and radius R, with f(c) ≠ 0 and |f(z)| ≤ M on the boundary. The sum of zero orders on the closed r-disc is at most log(M/|f(c)|)/log(R/r).
items.note: Exact specialization of AnalyticOnNhd.sum_divisor_le, JensenFormula.lean:390. A bound 0<M<1 requires rescaling f first. Divisors count multiplicities; this is not an arbitrary set-cardinality theorem.

items.name: Proposition 23 (zeros from maximum ratio)
items.statement: For f not identically zero and holomorphic on D̄ with M = max_{D̄}|f| and m = max_{D̄²}|f|, #{z ∈ D² : f(z) = 0} ≤ C log(M/m).
items.locator: Proposition 23, p.16, citing [30], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Follows from the library Jensen inequality by moving the centre to a point of maximal modulus on D̄² and covering. Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Complex Crofton formula
items.statement: vol(V ∩ B) = const(n) ∫_{G(n, codim V)} #(V ∩ B ∩ L) dL over complex linear subspaces of complementary dimension ([19, Prop. 14.6.3]).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2, (57), p.17, citing Chirka [19], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Proposition 24 (expansion on a Weierstrass polydisc)
items.statement: For a Weierstrass polydisc Δ for X of dimension m and F ∈ O(Δ̄), on Δ² one has F = Σ_{α ∈ ℕ^m × {0,…,e(X,Δ)−1}^{n−m}} c_α x^α + Q with Q vanishing on Δ² ∩ X and ‖c_α x^α‖_{Δ²} = O(2^{−|α|}‖F‖_Δ).
items.locator: Proposition 24, pp.17–18, citing [12, Thm. 3] and [11, Prop. 8], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Lemma 25 (approximate Thue–Siegel lemma)
items.statement: For a real μ×ν matrix A with μ,ν≥1 and integer N≥1, there is v∈Z^ν\{0} with ||v||∞≤N+1 and ||Av||∞≤N^((μ−ν)/μ)||A||∞, using the induced row-sum matrix infinity norm. The exact integer-kernel Siegel lemma has a different input and conclusion.
items.locator: Lemma 25, p.18, citing Waldschmidt [51, Lemma 4.11], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Mathlib has the exact integer Siegel lemma `Int.Matrix.exists_ne_zero_int_vec_norm_le` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/SiegelsLemma.lean:155), not this real Dirichlet-box version. Routed to DT.0 as a source. The original-source norm convention and box-bound endpoints must be checked before accepting this source route.

items.name: Lemma 26 (an interpolating polynomial)
items.statement: For d≥1, N≥2 there is P ∈ ℤ[y₁,…,y_{m+1}] ∖ {0} of degree ≤ d and coefficients ≤ N with ‖(P∘Φ)|_{X ∩ Δ²}‖ ≤ poly(d)^E max(1,‖Φ‖_Δ)^d (N log N) 2^{−d(E^{−1} log N)^{1/(m+1)}}, E = e(X,Δ)^{n−m}.
items.locator: Lemma 26 and proof, pp.18–19, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: State the nontrivial parameter range and normalize function norms. The constants in the small-value exponent and the tail summation in (68) need verification from the original interpolation sources; route 6 is not accepted. E22 records the N=1 counterexample.

items.name: Lemma 27 (Liouville-type lower bound)
items.statement: For P∈Z[y1,…,y_(m+1)] of total degree d≥0, coefficients bounded by N≥1, and algebraic tuple y with P(y)≠0, the product formula gives |P(y)|≥((d+1)^(m+1) N H_max(y)^(d(m+1)))^(−[Q(y):Q]). This conservative monomial-count bound suffices for Proposition 28.
items.locator: Lemma 27, p.19, citing Habegger [29, Lemma 14], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Corrected E21. The original d^(m+1) coefficient count is false for a fifth root of unity. The product formula proves the stated (d+1) bound, including degree zero.

items.name: Proposition 28 (interpolation of algebraic points)
items.statement: The set (Δ² ∩ X)(g, h; Φ) lies in the zero locus of P∘Φ with P ∈ ℤ[y] ∖ {0}, deg P ≪ g·E·(1+gh+log^+‖Φ‖_Δ)^m and h(P) ≪ E·(1+gh+log^+‖Φ‖_Δ)^{m+1}.
items.locator: Proposition 28 and proof, p.19, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Specify g≥1, h≥0, finite Weierstrass degree e≥1, bounded holomorphic Φ and Δ̄ in its domain. The estimates are upper bounds, with lower cutoffs; /29 constants remain to be checked.

items.name: Proposition 29 (inductive step for Theorem 3)
items.statement: If W ⊂ ℂ^ℓ is an irreducible Q-variety of positive dimension with ε = dist(B, Σ(V, W)) > 0, there are irreducible Q-subvarieties of codimension 1 W_α ⊂ W covering W ∩ A(g,h) with #{W_α}, max δ_{W_α} = poly(δ_ξ, δ_V, δ_W, δ_Φ, g, h, log ε^{-1}).
items.locator: Proposition 29 and proof, p.20, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Uses joint degree /56 and Q-blocks. The complete-intersection reduction invoked on p.20 needs the corrected /23, which remains a proof gap.

items.name: Theorem 6 (effective simultaneous torsion on elliptic squares)
items.statement: Let T be the fibred square of the Legendre family and C ⊂ T an irreducible curve over K with non-constant λ and no identical relation nP = mQ, (n,m) ∈ Z² \ {(0,0)}. At any c ∈ C with P(c), Q(c) both torsion, their orders are effectively bounded by poly(δ_C, [K:ℚ]); the set of such points is computable in polynomial time.
items.locator: Theorem 6, pp.20–21; proof §8, pp.22–28, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6 (misprints E4–E5)
items.note: The relation must allow all integer signs, including P=−Q; see E18. Effective polynomial dependence is a stated target, with the counting proof gaps explicitly retained.

items.name: Picard–Fuchs equations for Legendre periods and elliptic logarithms
items.statement: For Eλ:y²=x(x−1)(x−λ), λ away from 0,1 and the chosen section singularities, periods of dx/y satisfy L I=0 for L=λ(1−λ)∂λ²+(1−2λ)∂λ−1/4. For a local section x=x(λ), put q=1/y. Its elliptic logarithm I=∫∞^x(λ) q dx satisfies L I=B+(1/2)y/(x−λ)², where B=λ(1−λ)(2qλ x′+qx(x′)²+q x′′)+(1−2λ)q x′, evaluated at the section. Work on a simply connected regular branch with compatible integration paths.
items.locator: §8.1, (87) and (90), pp.22–23 (published version); boundary term expanded by the chain rule
items.note: The source’s boundary term B is spelled out by twice differentiating the moving-endpoint integral. The total-exact-differential identity is checked algebraically. PS.8 receives this specific Picard–Fuchs calculation; import relative Gauss–Manin comparison from ComplexComparisonPartII:C5. The counting-specific principal-bundle construction is /89.

items.name: Torsion order in terms of parameter height and degree
items.statement: Under the nondependent sections hypotheses of Theorem 6, if P(c) or Q(c) has torsion order n then n≤poly(δC,[Q(λ(c)):Q],h(λ(c))).
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Zimmer's explicit Néron–Tate versus Weil height estimates
items.statement: For an elliptic curve with a specified Weierstrass equation, compare its naive x-coordinate height and twice its Néron–Tate height, with an explicit error in the heights of the coefficients; include the corresponding function-field estimate used in Lemma 31. Fix the absolute-height normalization before using the error bound.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 31, p.24; §10.3, pp.32–33, citing Zimmer [56], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: RP.0 is the supplier of the explicit height-comparison adapter. The pinned Tau Ceti canonicalHeight and bounded-difference theorem already exist, but their existential constant does not give Zimmer’s explicit coefficient dependence. Faltings/Legendre comparison has been separated as /54.

items.name: Lemma 35 (growth of periods and logarithms on the leaf)
items.statement: For λ ∈ D^{1/2}, |f|, |f′|, |g|, |g′|, |z|, |z′|, |w|, |w′|, 1/Im(f/g) ≤ e^{poly(δ_C)}; so the ball lies in M_R with log R = poly(δ_C).
items.locator: §8.4, Lemma 35, pp.24–26, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Theorem 9 along chains of discs, and Schwarz–Pick for f/g. Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Masser–Zannier functional transcendence for periods and logarithms
items.statement: For the nonconstant Legendre family and two sections independent over Z as in Theorem 6, the two elliptic logarithms are algebraically independent over the field obtained by adjoining the periods to the algebraic function field of the base curve. Import the precise functional-transcendence statement [38, Lemma 5.1] with its base field and branch conventions.
items.locator: Lemmas 36–37 and proofs, pp.26–27, citing [38, Lemma 5.1], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: [38] is Masser–Zannier 2012, not the 2010 paper in the old prerequisite list. The weaker phrase “not algebraic” did not provide the algebraic independence used on p.27. This import still requires reading the original lemma before this route can be accepted. Local consequences are /70 and /71.

items.name: Theorem 7 (polynomial André–Oort for ℂⁿ)
items.statement: For V ⊂ ℂⁿ over K, the degrees of all maximal special subvarieties and the discriminants of their special coordinates are bounded by poly_n(δ_V, [K:ℚ]) (implied constant ineffective, from Siegel); there is an algorithm computing all maximal special subvarieties in poly_n(δ_V, [K:ℚ]) steps.
items.locator: Theorem 7, p.21; proof §9, pp.28–31, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6 (misprint E3)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: The j-function as a solution of a Schwarzian equation
items.statement: On a connected local domain, for f holomorphic with f′≠0 and f avoiding 0,1728, set χ(f)=S(f)+R(f)(f′)², R(f)=(f²−1968f+2654208)/(2f²(f−1728)²). Its solutions are locally f(τ)=j(g^−1τ) for a Möbius transformation with g^−1τ in H. The vector field in (115) on the regular locus and its n-fold product encode these solution graphs.
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Modular Ax–Lindemann (Pila)
items.statement: Let V⊂C^n be algebraic, and let an irreducible complex algebraic W have a nonempty analytic branch in H^n mapping into V under J=(j,…,j). Modular Ax–Lindemann places this branch in a pre-weakly-special variety W′ with J(W′∩H^n)⊂V. For the block consequence assume dim W>0.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 39, p.29, citing Pila [45], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Use a branch or connected analytic component, not an algebraic subset literally contained in H^n. Import the exact Pila 2011 Ax–Lindemann statement; /75 excludes points from V^ws.

items.name: Effective weakly special locus (Binyamini)
items.statement: The positive-dimensional weakly special locus V^ws is effectively computable with δ(V^ws) = poly_n(δ_V), and computing maximal special subvarieties reduces to special points outside V^ws of poly_n(δ_V) auxiliary varieties ([8, Thm. 4]).
items.locator: §9.2, p.29, citing [8, Thm. 4], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Use /75; the empty positive-dimensional locus for a zero-dimensional V is necessary. Source issue E17.

items.name: Nearby blocks lie close to the weakly special locus
items.statement: For a fixed precompact ξ-ball B in the standard j-leaf and a positive-dimensional irreducible algebraic block W from a sufficiently nearby leaf at distance ε, J(W∩πτ(B)) is contained in the O_B(ε)-neighbourhood of the positive-dimensional V^ws.
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Heights of CM points
items.statement: For a CM tuple p=(p1,…,pn), let Δ(p)=sum_i |disc End(E_pi)|. For every ε>0, h_max(p)≤C(n,ε) Δ(p)^ε, using Chowla–Selberg and logarithmic-derivative bounds.
items.locator: (121), p.30, citing [28, Lemma 4.1] and Tsimerman [50, Cor. 3.3], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Corrected the product to the sum printed in (120), p.29. Quantitative CM-height arithmetic must be imported from the CM-height direction already proposed by PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18, not rebuilt in this counting Part II; a concrete current supplier stage is still required.

items.name: Duke's equidistribution of CM points
items.statement: For a single modular curve, full Galois orbits of CM points equidistribute for normalized hyperbolic area as the order discriminant tends to infinity. For the application choose a compact continuity set K0⊂Ω with measure >1−1/(4n), enlarge it by the finitely many small-discriminant CM representatives, and set K=K0^n. The marginal Duke estimates and a union bound then place at least 2/3 of each sufficiently large CM tuple orbit in K. This does not assert product equidistribution or the same property for an arbitrary K of product measure 2/3.
items.locator: §9.3, p.30, citing Duke [23], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: GN.4 supplies the one-coordinate Duke theorem. The elementary marginal/union-bound adapter repairs the use on p.30; source issue E14.

items.name: Siegel's lower bound for class numbers (Brauer–Siegel)
items.statement: For any ε>0, imaginary quadratic orders of negative discriminant D have h(D) ≥ cε |D|^(1/2−ε), with ineffective cε>0. The ring-class-field theorem and marginal orbit projection imply [Q(p):Q] ≥ c(n,ε) max_i |Di|^(1/2−ε), hence a positive power bound in Δ(p)=sum_i|Di| for large Δ.
items.locator: (126), p.30, citing Brauer–Siegel [18], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: AN.4 supplies the analytic lower-bound input. Import the nonmaximal-order class-number formula and CM.3 ring-class-field action; do not infer this orbit statement from the analytic class-number formula alone.

items.name: Theorem 8 (Galois orbits of torsion points, after Schmidt)
items.statement: For an elliptic curve E over K and a torsion point p ∈ E(K̄) of order n, n = poly([K:ℚ], h_Fal(E), [K(p):K]).
items.locator: Theorem 8, p.21; proof §§10.1, 10.3, pp.31–34, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6 (misprint E6)
items.note: Lemmas 44–47: cover by poly(h) ξ′-balls, count the multiples p, p², …, pⁿ on the graph of the uniformization via Theorem 3. Previously due to David by transcendence. Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Sketch for principally polarized abelian varieties (§10.4)
items.statement: Conditional extension of the §10.3 counting argument: for principally polarized A/K of fixed dimension g, the stated target is n≤poly_g([K:Q],[K(p):K],1+max(0,h_Fal(A))) for torsion p of order n. The sketch requires a uniform poly_g(height) covering by suitable complex polydiscs, which §10.4 explicitly says is work in progress; it is not a proved theorem of this paper.
items.locator: §10.4, p.34, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6 (a sketch)
items.note: Import theta/Faltings comparisons from R35.5 and the existing abelian-variety/moduli owners. Acquire a published covering theorem with exactly the needed quantitative domain control before scheduling this proof.

items.name: Lemma 48 (Gronwall for monic linear ODEs)
items.statement: On the unit disc centred at 0, let L=∂^n+a1∂^(n−1)+…+an with n≥1, coefficients holomorphic near the closed disc, |aj|≤A and |b|≤B. Set J=(f,…,f^(n−1)). For Lf=b, Gronwall on radial paths gives ||J(t)||≤exp(Cn(1+A))(||J(0)||+B). The nth derivative is then bounded using the differential equation. For a general radius retain path-length and derivative-rescaling factors.
items.locator: Lemma 48 and proof, p.35, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Corrected Lemma 48 using E13. Import /65; do not rebuild Gronwall or apply an n×n companion matrix to an (n+1)-entry jet.

items.name: Effective upper bound for invariant slope
items.statement: For a Fuchsian operator L over a number field, with the rational coefficient norm and literal pullback of /72, invariantAngle(L)≤exp(poly_n(δL)); this uses the finiteness theorem [14, Proposition 32] and effective semialgebraic bounds.
items.locator: Definition 49, Propositions 50–51, p.36, citing [14], Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6 (Proposition 51 needs a normalization, sourceIssues E8; misprint E7)
items.note: Proposition 50 only. The normalization-sensitive leading-coefficient lower bound is /73. Rational-coefficient versus polynomial-normalized slope comparison must be made explicit in the blueprint.

items.name: Lemma 52 (rational functions on discs)
items.statement: Let D be the unit disc and r a reduced rational function, with ||r|| equal to the ratio of coefficient l1 norms. If r has no poles in the doubled disc D^(1/2), then sup_D |r|≤exp(C deg r)||r||; if it has no zeros there, then inf_D |r|≥exp(−C deg r)||r|| (at regular evaluation points).
items.locator: Lemma 52 and proof, pp.36–37, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6
items.note: Routed to the new Part II EffectivePointCountingOnFoliations.

items.name: Theorem 9 (growth for inhomogeneous Fuchsian equations)
items.statement: Assume L and L+1 are Fuchsian with the normalization of /72–73, and defined over a number field. For D=Dr(t0) with its double disc avoiding Σ, put z=(t−t0)/r. If Lf=b and |b|≤B on the double disc, the natural-coordinate jet through order n satisfies ||j_z^n f(t1)||≤exp(cL)(B+||j_z^n f(t0)||), cL=exp(poly_n(δL)), for t1∈D. Iteration along a controlled chain of discs yields growth polynomial in inverse distance with an additive contribution of the forcing b as well as the initial jet.
items.locator: Theorem 9 and proof, p.37, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e6 (holds under the normalization of sourceIssues E8)
items.note: E8 normalization is now in the statement, not only the locator. Use the n-dimensional companion jet through order n−1 and recover derivative n from the equation (E13); retain the forcing term in chaining (E16).

items.name: Absolute-height formula and coordinate-maximum convention
items.statement: For algebraic x with primitive irreducible minimal polynomial a0 product_i(T-x_i) in Z[T] and positive leading coefficient, h_abs(x)=(log a0 + sum_i log max(1,|x_i|))/d. For a finite tuple define h_max to be the maximum of the scalar absolute heights (0 for the empty tuple); this is the convention in A(g,h), not the relative projective height.
items.note: The absolute scalar height exists. Its minimal-polynomial comparison API was not found in the pinned tree. Import the common height normalization from DT.0; RP.0 is a consumer.

items.name: Legendre parameter versus stable Faltings height
items.statement: After a bounded-degree extension putting E in Legendre form, bound h(λ) in terms of 1+max(0,h_Fal(E)) and the field degree, and bound h_Fal(Eλ) in terms of h(λ). The reverse comparison h(λ)≪1+max(0,h_Fal(E)) (with the stated normalization and allowable field extension) is the direction needed to turn the h=max(h(λ),[K:Q]) bound in §10.3 into Theorem 8.
items.note: The published sentence writes only the forward bound. The extraction must record the reverse supplier and the degree at most six for ordering the 2-torsion points; this review does not certify an unstated constant. Ordering the 2-torsion requires degree at most six; an additional quadratic extension can remove the twist to obtain the displayed Legendre equation, so degree at most twelve suffices for the full presentation.

items.name: Bad locus for algebraic blocks and a map
items.statement: For irreducible algebraic W⊂C^ℓ, Σ(V,W;Φ) consists of regular leaf points p where the germ Φ on Lp∩V is not finite, or its image contains an analytic component of the germ of W at Φ(p); include the foliation singular locus when using global distance estimates. Germs and the finite-map condition refer to the chosen analytic branch.

api.name: BlockBadLocus.nonfinite_mem
api.statement: Failure of finiteness of the map germ places the base point in Σ(V,W;Φ).

api.name: BlockBadLocus.component_mem
api.statement: With a finite map germ, membership means its image contains an analytic component of W at Φ(p).

api.name: BlockBadLocus.singular_mem
api.statement: For the global distance convention, singular foliation points belong to the bad locus.

unitTests.name: BlockBadLocus.test_identity_line
unitTests.statement: For V=M=C, Φ=id and W=C with the full leaf, every point is in the block bad locus.

unitTests.name: BlockBadLocus.test_constant_map
unitTests.statement: A constant map from a positive-dimensional leaf germ is nonfinite, hence bad.

unitTests.name: BlockBadLocus.test_transverse_curve
unitTests.statement: For Φ(z)=(z,0), V=C and W={x=0} at 0, the map is finite and its horizontal image contains no component of the vertical W germ.

uses.how: Separates the two reasons a block may persist on a nearby leaf.

items.name: Algebraic points of bounded joint degree and height
items.statement: For A⊂C^ℓ, A(g,h) consists of p∈A∩Qbar^ℓ with [Q(p1,…,pℓ):Q]≤g and max_i h_abs(pi)≤h. For an analytic map Φ define A(g,h;Φ) by the same conditions on Φ(p). It uses one compositum field, not a coordinatewise degree bound.

api.name: BoundedAlgebraicPoints.mem_iff
api.statement: Membership requires the joint compositum degree and the maximum scalar height bounds.

api.name: BoundedAlgebraicPoints.mono
api.statement: Enlarging A, g or h enlarges A(g,h).

api.name: BoundedAlgebraicPoints.map_version
api.statement: A(g,h;Φ) is the inverse image of the bounded algebraic tuples under Φ, restricted to A.

unitTests.name: BoundedAlgebraicPoints.test_rational_pair
unitTests.statement: For g=1, every admitted tuple has all coordinates rational.

unitTests.name: BoundedAlgebraicPoints.test_independent_quadratics
unitTests.statement: The tuple (√2,√3) is not admitted with g=2, although both coordinates individually have degree 2.

unitTests.name: BoundedAlgebraicPoints.test_height_zero
unitTests.statement: The tuple (0,1,−1) is admitted with g=1 and h=0 when it belongs to A.

uses.how: Prevents replacing joint degree by coordinatewise degree.

items.name: Rational coordinates of simultaneous torsion points
items.statement: Under the hypotheses and the chosen disc/branch of Lemma 33, for Rhat=exp(poly(δC)), each conjugate cσ in that branch determines a rational matrix U in (z,w)=(f,g)U. Its coordinate denominators are at most the respective torsion orders and its logarithmic height is poly(δC,log n); the matrix lies in the counting domain A⊂Mat2x2(R).

items.name: Growth on the elliptic uniformization charts
items.statement: In §10.3, h=max(h(λ),[K:Q]) and δ=exp(−poly(h)). On each selected doubled x-disc away from {0,1,λ,∞}, a chosen branch of y and a chosen normalized primitive z=∫dx/y yield a ξ′=ξ/y leaf ball contained in an ambient ball of radius exp(poly(h)). The initial lift must have the same bound.

items.name: Many bounded-height torsion points on one chart
items.statement: For a point p of order n, with N(p)=[K(p):K], the Galois conjugates of its multiples contain at least n/2 distinct torsion points of order at most n, height poly(h), degree over K at most N(p), and x-coordinate in Λδ. One of the poly(h) discs and one y-branch contains at least n/poly(h) of them. Use the Galois-stable union of the multiples and its orbits, counting distinct points.

items.name: Algebraic blocks in the elliptic covering graph
items.statement: For the foliation on E×Cz×C²u×C²ω in §10.3 with V={z=u1ω1+u2ω2} and Φ=(x,y,u1,u2), any positive-dimensional irreducible block from a leaf has u1ω1+u2ω2 constant. Otherwise it would make a nonconstant elliptic function algebraic over its covering coordinate.

items.name: Height and joint degree of elliptic torsion lifts
items.statement: Every point selected in Lemma 45 lifts to A⊂C²×R² with log-height poly(h,log n) and joint field degree at most [K:Q]N(p). The u-coordinates are rational with denominators at most n; the x,y coordinates lie in the field of the chosen torsion point.

items.name: Degree and height of CM representatives
items.statement: For a CM tuple p in C^n, its representative τ in Ω^n has each coordinate imaginary quadratic, joint degree [Q(τ):Q]≤2^n and H_max(τ)≤poly_n(Δ(p)), where Δ is the sum of absolute order discriminants. Use g=2^n in Theorem 3.
items.locator: (127), p.30 and application p.31; corrected E15 (published version)

items.name: Metric packing-covering comparisons
items.statement: In a metric space, with packing at strict separation and covering by closed balls, S(A,2ε)≤N(A,ε)≤S(A,ε) for ε≥0, allowing infinity. Specialize the extended-natural counts to finite values on the compact sets used by the paper.
items.note: CoveringNumbers.lean:128,330,354 at 082e2d3; names checked in the namespace. Combine the first inequality with externalCoveringNumber≤coveringNumber.

items.name: Schwarz–Pick metric contraction
items.statement: A holomorphic self-map of the unit disc, represented as a map of PoincareDisc, does not increase Poincaré distance. Apply by disc/half-plane coordinate changes to the period ratio f/g in (100).
items.note: SchwarzPick.lean:132 at f790474. The period-ratio and coordinate-change application still belongs to /37.

items.name: Norm Gronwall inequality
items.statement: If a normed-space-valued function is continuous on [a,b], has a right derivative there, has initial norm ≤δ, and satisfies ||f′(t)||≤K||f(t)||+ε, then ||f(t)||≤gronwallBound δ K ε (t−a).
items.note: Gronwall.lean:134 at 082e2d3. The complex path and companion-system adapter is /49.

items.name: Chow–van der Waerden equations with complexity control
items.statement: A K-subvariety V admits a set-theoretic defining collection P1,…,PS with δ(Pα)≤poly(δV), where S depends only on the fixed ambient dimension; heights are measured in Chow coordinates.

items.name: Arithmetic complexity of a multiplicity operator
items.statement: For a basic operator of order k applied to P along commuting rational vector fields ξ, δ(M^(k)P)≤poly(δP,δξ,k), on the regular localized chart. The determinant size and derivative orders give the bound.

items.name: Multiplicity detected by basic operators
items.statement: For a holomorphic n-tuple F and k≥0, its local intersection multiplicity is >k if and only if every basic multiplicity operator of order k vanishes. Use multiplicity infinity for nonisolated common zeros and 0 outside the zero set.

items.name: Analytic resultant on a finite Weierstrass projection
items.statement: For a curve Γ with finite proper projection Γ∩Δ→Dz of degree μ and G holomorphic near Δ, define RΔ,Γ(G)(z) as the product of G(z,w) over the fibre, with analytic multiplicities. This is holomorphic, including at branch values.

api.name: AnalyticResultant.fibre_product
api.statement: At an unramified fibre the resultant is the product of the values at all sheets.

api.name: AnalyticResultant.multiplicative
api.statement: R(GH)=R(G)R(H) with multiplicities.

api.name: AnalyticResultant.holomorphic
api.statement: The product extends holomorphically across branch values for the finite proper projection.

unitTests.name: AnalyticResultant.test_ramified_square
unitTests.statement: On Γ={w²=z}, R(w)(z)=−z.

unitTests.name: AnalyticResultant.test_remote_zero_sheet
unitTests.statement: For Γ={w=0 or w=1/4}, R(z(w−1/4)) is identically zero, even if the pair of defining functions has an isolated zero at the origin.

uses.how: Transfers zero counting to the base disc without losing a sheet or a multiplicity.

items.name: Finiteness of the Betti-coordinate map on every leaf
items.statement: In the principal G-bundle of §8.1 and enlarged space of §8.5, the germ Φ=U on each leaf intersected with V={(z,w)=(f,g)U} is finite. A positive-dimensional fibre contradicts the Masser–Zannier functional-transcendence input; transfer from the standard leaf by G-equivariance.

items.name: Blocks have fixed base parameter in the elliptic square
items.statement: A positive-dimensional irreducible algebraic block from the standard leaf in §8.5 lies in {(z(λ0),w(λ0))=(f(λ0),g(λ0))U} for a single λ0 in the selected domain. Since f/g is nonreal, each such affine space has at most one real matrix point; sufficiently nearby leaves retain this property.
items.locator: Lemma 37 and following paragraph, pp.26–27 (published version)

items.name: Slope and invariant slope of a rational differential operator
items.statement: For L=sum_{j=0}^n a_j(t)∂^(n−j), a0≠0, let ||p/q||=||p||1/||q||1 for a reduced rational function. Define angle(L)=max_{1≤j≤n}||aj||/||a0|| and invariantAngle(L)=sup_{φ∈Aut(P1)}angle(φ*L). The pullback is the operator acting on f∘φ, with no arbitrary scalar renormalization.

api.name: DifferentialSlope.rational_norm
api.statement: Use the ratio of coefficient l1 norms in a reduced numerator and denominator.

api.name: DifferentialSlope.slope_eq
api.statement: The slope is the maximum of the n lower coefficient norms divided by the leading norm.

api.name: DifferentialSlope.pullback
api.statement: Compute the literal operator under Möbius change of variable; do not independently rescale its leading coefficient.

unitTests.name: DifferentialSlope.test_derivative_slope
unitTests.statement: For L=∂t, angle(L)=0.

unitTests.name: DifferentialSlope.test_euler_slope
unitTests.statement: For L=t∂t+1, angle(L)=1.

unitTests.name: DifferentialSlope.test_scaling_leading
unitTests.statement: For φ(s)=κs, a0(φ*∂t)=κ^−1, so a universal positive lower bound requires additional hypotheses.

uses.how: Makes the normalization relevant to the forcing term explicit.

items.name: Lower bound for pulled-back leading coefficients with normalization
items.statement: Assume L and L+1 are Fuchsian, L is defined over a number field, and the literal pullback/coefficient norm convention of /72 is fixed. Then inf_{φ∈Aut(P1)}||a0(φ*L)||≥exp(−poly_n(δL)). The extra assumption excludes L=∂t and applies to the Legendre operator λ(1−λ)∂²+(1−2λ)∂−1/4.
items.note: The review confirms the counterexample and the needed normalization. A detailed reduced-rational-coefficient norm comparison remains part of the source-complete proof obligation.

items.name: Jets for the companion system
items.statement: For a holomorphic scalar f and integer n≥1, the companion vector is J_n f=(f,f′,…,f^(n−1)) in C^n. The full n-jet is j^n f=(f,…,f^n) in C^(n+1). Under t=t0+rz the derivative of order j is multiplied by r^j; do not identify these two vectors.
items.locator: Appendix A, (147)–(150), p.35; corrected E13 (published version)

api.name: CompanionJet.coordinate
api.statement: The jth coordinate of J_n f is f^(j), for 0≤j<n.

api.name: CompanionJet.companion_equation
api.statement: For monic order-n L, J_n solves the n×n companion first-order system.

api.name: CompanionJet.change_scale
api.statement: Under t=t0+rz, the jth derivative becomes r^j times the original derivative.

unitTests.name: CompanionJet.test_order_one
unitTests.statement: J_1 f contains only f, while j^1 f contains f and f′.

unitTests.name: CompanionJet.test_scaled_quadratic
unitTests.statement: For f(t)=t² and t=rz, the second derivative in z is 2r².

uses.how: Avoids the matrix-size error and tracks radius powers.

items.name: Positive-dimensional weakly special locus
items.statement: For V⊂Y(1)^n, V^ws is the union of its positive-dimensional weakly special subvarieties. A weakly special subvariety is obtained by fixing coordinates and imposing modular relations in disjoint coordinate blocks. Excluding zero-dimensional weakly special points is essential: otherwise V^ws=V.

api.name: PositiveWeaklySpecialLocus.mem_iff
api.statement: Membership means lying on a positive-dimensional weakly special subvariety contained in V.

api.name: PositiveWeaklySpecialLocus.subset
api.statement: V^ws is a subset of V.

api.name: PositiveWeaklySpecialLocus.monotone
api.statement: For V⊂W, V^ws⊂W^ws.

unitTests.name: PositiveWeaklySpecialLocus.test_point_empty
unitTests.statement: For a singleton V, V^ws is empty.

unitTests.name: PositiveWeaklySpecialLocus.test_whole_modular_line
unitTests.statement: For V=Y(1), V^ws=V.

unitTests.name: PositiveWeaklySpecialLocus.test_diagonal
unitTests.statement: For V={(x,x)}⊂Y(1)², V^ws=V.

uses.how: Defines the locus removed to leave isolated special points.

items.name: Restricted elementary o-minimal structure
items.statement: R_RE expands the ordered real field by exp restricted to [0,1] and sin restricted to [0,π], with fixed conventions outside those intervals. “Definable” allows parameters, so constants in Theorem 4 may depend on the definable set.

api.name: RestrictedElementary.restricted_exp
api.statement: On [0,1], the named restricted exponential agrees with the real exponential.

api.name: RestrictedElementary.restricted_sin
api.statement: On [0,π], the named restricted sine agrees with real sine.

items.name: Polynomial reparametrization of a foliation
items.statement: On the determinant-nonzero locus of M_D×C^n_s×M, with Φ fixed on each leaf, set P_D(ξ)_i=∂si+sum_j(∂Φj/∂si)ξj. The chart is (Φ,a+x,φp(Φ(a+x)−Φ(a))). The projection to M reparametrizes the original leaf.

api.statement: The chart projects to φp(Φ(a+x)−Φ(a)).

items.name: A small rational point outside a proper variety
items.statement: For a proper closed subvariety Z⊊A^N of total degree ≤d, d≥1, there exists x∈Q^N\Z with ||x||∞≤1 and coordinate-maximum multiplicative height H(x)≤d. Slice successively with rational coordinates; properness and d≥1 are necessary.

items.name: Codimension of bad polynomial reparametrizations
items.statement: For p outside ΣV, fixed full-rank A and a, the proposed Lemma 19 bound is that the polynomial reparametrizations producing improper intersection have codimension at least D on the invertible-Jacobian parameter locus. The polynomial image parameterization of (46) must be used. A proof with this parameterization is missing: (49) uses inverse images instead.
items.note: Do not schedule the printed proof as an established lemma. Repair the incidence family and prove the claimed codimension, including passage to the determinant-nonzero locus.

items.name: Most CM conjugates avoid the weakly special locus quantitatively
items.statement: For special p∈V\V^ws and ε>0, at least two-thirds of its Galois conjugates over the field of definition satisfy log^+ dist(pσ,V^ws)^−1 ≤poly_n(δV) Oε(Δ(p)^ε). Use a polynomial vanishing on V^ws but not p, bounds for its value and for the absolute sizes of pσ, and the mean-value inequality.

items.name: Height bound for a torsion specialization
items.statement: For the curve and sections of Theorem 6, if P(c) or Q(c) is torsion then h(λ(c))≤poly(δC), with absolute logarithmic height.

items.name: Many conjugates stay away from singular parameters
items.statement: With the finite algebraic exceptional set Σ in §8.1 and λ∉Σ, for δ=2^−poly(δC,h(λ)) at least half the Galois conjugates of λ lie in Λδ={|λ|<δ^−1, |λ−σ|>δ for all σ∈Σ}. Work over the field defining the data or account for its degree.

items.name: One disc and branch contain many conjugates
items.statement: For a simultaneous torsion specialization c, a logarithmic cover of Λδ by poly(δC) discs, with expanded discs away from Σ, has one disc and one branch of C containing at least [Q(c):Q]/poly(δC) conjugates in the Q-defined presentation of §8.

items.name: A small Weierstrass polydisc from a multiplicity operator
items.statement: For n−1 holomorphic functions bounded by 1 on the unit ball and a nonzero order-k multiplicity operator in the w-variables at 0, construct a standard-coordinate Weierstrass polydisc for their zero set whose logarithmic reciprocal radii are bounded polynomially in k and log(1/s), with size parameters bounded below. Its radii may be decreased within the construction to satisfy the local ball restriction needed by /15, but quantitative compatibility must be proved.

items.name: A nonvanishing multiplicity operator has a distance bound
items.statement: For a complete intersection V=V(P1,…,Pn) on a fixed bounded regular chart and p outside ΣV, there is a basic multiplicity operator of order k≤poly(degξ,degP) with log|Mp^(k)P|≥−poly(δξ,δP)(1+log^+dist(p,ΣV)^−1). To replace δP by δV, first choose and prove a bound for normalized defining equations.
items.note: Corrected E23: rescaling defining equations leaves V unchanged but rescales all multiplicity determinants. Propagate the equation-height bound through the general-position and complete-intersection construction.

items.name: Covering the circle saturation
items.statement: For A in the unit ball of C^n and ε>0, N(S¹·A,2ε)≤(1+floor(π/ε))N(A,ε). Multiply an ε-net of A by an ε-net of the unit circle.

items.name: A Weierstrass polydisc controlled by volume
items.statement: For a pure m-dimensional analytic subset X of the unit ball with finite volume, construct a Weierstrass polydisc Δ containing a concentric ball of reciprocal radius poly_n(1+vol X) and with degree e(X,Δ)≤poly_n(1+vol X). For m=n use the full-dimensional trivial projection; for m<n use the complementary-ball induction.

items.name: The elliptic-square Picard–Fuchs principal bundle
items.statement: On the regular part of C, form M=C×G with G=Mat2x2⋊GL2 and (ML,MP)(NL,NP)=(ML+MP NL,MP NP). Encode the two period solutions in MP and the two inhomogeneous logarithm solutions in ML together with their first derivatives. The lifted λ-vector field given by the second-order equations defines a flat principal G-bundle under right multiplication. The standard leaf uses a period basis and logarithms of P,Q.

api.name: EllipticSquarePeriodBundle.leaf_translate
api.statement: Right translation changes the period basis by an invertible constant matrix and logarithms by constant period combinations.

api.name: EllipticSquarePeriodBundle.standard_leaf
api.statement: A compatible period basis and two elliptic logarithms determine the distinguished local horizontal leaf.

routes.reason: LD.6 builds Pila–Zannier-type applications from functional-transcendence theorems and records proven André–Oort cases. The paper uses two such theorems: Masser–Zannier's transcendence of elliptic logarithms over periods, and Pila's modular Ax–Lindemann. Both control the blocks coming from nearby leaves.

DT.0 owns Dirichlet approximation, DT.1 Liouville bounds and DT.3 the tools of transcendence theory. The paper uses Wilkie's real-matrix Thue–Siegel lemma, Habegger's Liouville-type lower bound for integer polynomials at algebraic points, and Brownawell's Diophantine Łojasiewicz inequality.

PS.8 receives the homogeneous Legendre Picard–Fuchs equation and its explicit moving-endpoint inhomogeneous calculation as a source-selected family calculation. Import general relative de Rham/Gauss–Manin comparison from ComplexComparisonPartII:C5; /89 keeps the counting-specific flat principal bundle in the counting extension.

RP.0 supplies the explicit coefficient-dependent and function-field height comparison, extending the pinned elliptic canonical-height API. The Faltings comparison is already planned by R35.5 and is imported as item /54.

AN.4 connects L-functions to the analytic class-number formula. Siegel's ineffective lower bound for class numbers of imaginary quadratic orders is the input that makes Theorem 7's constant ineffective.

routes.title: Logic, definability, valued fields and motivic integration, Part II: effective point counting on foliations
routes.reason: No atlas layer plans effective point counting: multiplicity operators, Weierstrass-polydisc coverings and polylogarithmic Pila–Wilkie bounds. This is a new direction for the definability roadmap, and the existing LogicAndDefinability Part IIs (Ax–Schanuel, finitely generated fields) have other subjects. The effective applications depend on Theorem 3, so they live here too. The direction is plausible, but the review has found proof and ownership blockers; this route is not ready to become a design job.

sourceIssues.printed: "Proposition 51. Suppose L is defined over a number field. Then inf_{φ ∈ Aut(ℙ¹)} ‖a₀(φ*L)‖ = e^{−poly_n(δ_L)}. Proof. … Now the operator L′ := L + 1 is also Fuchsian …"
sourceIssues.correction: For the proposed repair assume that L and L+1 are Fuchsian, and fix the literal pullback and reduced-rational-coefficient norm. This holds for the Legendre operator (87). Complete the rational-norm comparison and use the corrected companion-jet argument E13. Retain the inhomogeneous forcing when chaining estimates (E16). sourceIssues.reason: For a general Fuchsian operator, L + 1 need not be Fuchsian, and both statements fail. Take L = ∂_t, which is Fuchsian: its only singular point ∞ is regular singular (∂_t = −z(z∂_z), z = 1/t). Then φ(s) = κs gives φ*L = κ^{-1}∂_s and inf_φ ‖a₀(φ*L)‖ = 0. In Theorem 9 take b(t) = (t − t₀)/(2r) (|b| ≤ 1 on D^{1/2}) and f = (t − t₀)²/(4r), so j_z f(t₀) = 0 while |∂_z f(t₀ + r/2)| = r/4, unbounded in r. Here L + 1 = ∂ + 1 has an irregular singularity at ∞.
